title: 9 AI Platforms Breached in 1 Month - The AI Security Skill Companies Need
content:
In just 1 month, AT LEAST 9 AI developer platforms disclosed security incidents. This is the career skill nobody is talking about.
The security company Wiz published a report called Black October.
It lists at least 9 AI developer platforms that disclosed incidents this month, including Fireworks AI, Lightning AI, OpenCode, Railway, Warp and Northflank.
Wiz says the public reports show attackers hunting for stored environment variables, especially the ones that hold AI access keys.
Why AI keys? Because of something called LLMJACKING.
Attackers use stolen keys to run AI models, and the owner of the key pays the bill. Some even resell that access.
And the numbers here are wild.
In one case Wiz studied, a stolen key made about 800,000 Amazon Bedrock calls in about 30 hours.
In another, a single address made about 1.7 MILLION calls in about 13 hours.
BleepingComputer reports this added up to roughly 100,000 dollars in AI usage.
One platform, Zeabur, says it will shut down because of its incident.
So here is the career angle. Every company is plugging AI into its products, and very few people know how to secure it.
If you want to stand out, learn 3 THINGS.
1. Secrets management. Never hard-code keys, and rotate them on a schedule.
2. Spend alerts and limits on every AI account.
3. Least privilege. Give each key access only to the models and regions it really needs.
Say an interviewer asks you, "How would you protect our AI API keys?"
Most candidates talk about prompts. You talk about rotation, spend alerts and scoped keys. You just became the safer hire.
Here's my take.
AI security is where cloud security was 10 years ago. Early, messy, and SHORT OF PEOPLE.
Pick one of these 3 skills this week and set it up on your own project.
